Theme

Money, work & business

company noun

a business firm

also firm, corporation, partnership, a business, corporate, establishment (a business), business establishment, enterprise, business enterprise

classical

Cic. Sest. 32: nūlla Rōmae societās vectīgālium (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. corporation, company
Traupman 333
Traupman 315

societās, societātis f.

noun, third declension

a company, a partnership

Classically a partnership for trade, and the companies that farmed the public revenues; Morgan–Owens gives it for a modern company, and societās mercātōria for a trading one.

Other words

  • negōtium, negōtiī n. — a business, as an establishment

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 165

    Traupman’s word for “a business”; classically business, work, an affair (see business).

  • negōtiātiō, negōtiātiōnis f. — a business, a trading or banking concern

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. negōtiātiō: wholesale business, banking business; Traupman 165; Cic. Fam. 6.8.2: reliquiae Asiāticae negōtiātiōnis (Lewis & Short); Traupman 285

    Classically the business itself, the trade carried on; Traupman uses it of a business establishment with its premises.

Examples

  • numquam est fidēlis cum potente societās

    a partnership with the powerful is never to be trustedPhaedr. 1.5.1

  • Parva est societās nostra; decem tantum sumus.

    Ours is a small company; there are only ten of us.composed

See also business, goods, job.
